Sequence #25-ATTACH5-B Hybrid VTOL to Enable Operational Capabilities Description: The U.S. Army is soliciting critical data and insights on hybrid vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) and short take-off and landing (STOL) aircraft concepts. The Army is seeking to leverage industry expertise to W911W625R0006 0002 Page 6 of 8 inform Army decision-making regarding the feasibility, operational impact, cost of adoption, and requirements applicable to hybrid technologies for future Army missions. nable new modes of operation that enhance warfighter outcomes. This effort is intended to identify ways in which a hybrid VTOL/STOL solution could bring added value to Army operations. Develop and validate study insights through analysis, modeling, test data, and demonstrations. October 2022 CUI CUI PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) FOR Optimizing Human Weapon System (OHWS) Services 1.0 General: 1.1 Scope: The mission is accomplished by increasing the physical capacity of fighter aircrew, decreasing the rate of injuries, and accelerating return to duty. Contractor personnel will work with Air National Guard (ANG) fighter aircrew to optimize physical performance targeting neck and back pain prevention while monitoring, analyzing, and resolving physical readiness concerns. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished, to perform Massage Therapy and Preventive Physical Therapy Services, as defined in this PWS. 1.1.1 Objectives: The purpose of the OHWS program is to reduce the frequency and severity of neck and back pain injuries, reduce duty time lost, improve quality of life, enhance readiness, and support fighter aircrew retention. The contract services must, at a minimum, deliver the services identified in Section 4.0 of this PWS and use available facilities so personnel will have convenient access to the Contract specialists. The Contractor goal is to reduce injury rates and to increase the rate of fighter aircrew fully mission capable status. 1.2 Background: In 2019 Air Combat Command (ACC) published a new requirement, which supports Regular Air Force (RegAF) Combat Air Forces (CAF) fighter squadrons at locations in Air Combat Command (ACC), Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), and United States Air Forces Europe (USAFE). The contractor shall utilize streamlined maintenance and sustainment processes and procedures appropriately tailored for quick response actions that occur at the Wallops Range while also adhering to the CM processes implemented. RANGE OPERATIONS CONTRACT II ________________________________________________________________________ 29 The contractor shall establish a routine equipment preventative maintenance and readiness program that follows or exceeds manufacturer’s recommended procedures or the applicable sections of the Inter-Range Instrumentation Group (IRIG) Standards. Reference http://www.irig.org to obtain IRIG standards. The contractor shall define, document, and implement this program and recommend applicable standards to be utilized in support of the program. The contractor shall perform continuous system assessments necessary to provide effective maintenance and sustainment reporting at various reviews defined in Sections 3 and 4. The WFF currently utilizes the United States Air Force Instrumentation Radar Support Program (IRSP), which can be referenced at https://irsp.com/ , to perform varying Depot Level Maintenance (DLM) activities for Wallops Range radars and provide critical spares for radar

hat follows or exceeds manufacturer’s recommended procedures or the applicable sections of the Inter-Range Instrumentation Group (IRIG) Standards. Reference http://www.irig.org to obtain IRIG standards. The contractor shall define, document, and implement this program and recommend applicable standards to be utilized in support of the program. The contractor shall perform continuous system assessments necessary to provide effective maintenance and sustainment reporting at various reviews defined in Sections 3 and 4. The WFF currently utilizes the United States Air Force Instrumentation Radar Support Program (IRSP), which can be referenced at https://irsp.com/ , to perform varying Depot Level Maintenance (DLM) activities for Wallops Range radars and provide critical spares for radar systems. The contractor shall define how they propose to perform DLM activities for the range instrumentation systems along with the estimated costs per year to implement the approach and justification of the choice made. AOI 01: EF Technology Sprints - Activated Digital Thread for Battlefield Responsiveness AFRL is seeking innovative solutions to operationalize digital architecture capable of responding to battlefield dynamics in near real-time. The objective is to close the loop between battlefield data and the manufacturing floor, creating an adaptive manufacturing ecosystem that expedites the re-configuration of weapon systems to enhance warfighter lethality. Solutions are sought to drastically reduce design-to-field cycle times by addressing one or more of the following technical challenges: (1) Model-Based Quality Assurance & Digital Certification. Goal: Transition from physical-test-dependent to analysis-led certification. To realize surge manufacturing, the bottleneck of physical requalification for every design change must be eliminated. Solutions are sought that leverage Certification by Analysis (CbA) and probabilistic simulation to validate manufacturing variability and design changes. Approaches should address how seamless data interchange can support certification allowing for rapid acceptance of re-configured components without extensive physical testing campaigns. (2) Modular Integration & Factorial Manufacturing. Goal: Enable "Plug-and-Play"

Contractor personnel will work with Air National Guard (ANG) fighter aircrew to optimize physical performance targeting neck and back pain prevention while monitoring, analyzing, and resolving physical readiness concerns. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished, to perform Massage Therapy and Preventive Physical Therapy Services, as defined in this PWS. 1.1.1 Objectives: The purpose of the OHWS program is to reduce the frequency and severity of neck and back pain injuries, reduce duty time lost, improve quality of life, enhance readiness, and support fighter aircrew retention. The contract services must, at a minimum, deliver the services identified in Section 4.0 of this PWS and use available facilities so personnel will have convenient access to the Contract specialists. The Contractor goal is to reduce injury rates and to increase the rate of fighter aircrew fully mission capable status. 1.2 Background: In 2019 Air Combat Command (ACC) published a new requirement, which supports Regular Air Force (RegAF) Combat Air Forces (CAF) fighter squadrons at locations in Air Combat Command (ACC), Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), and United States Air Forces Europe (USAFE). The instrumentation systems that make up the Wallops Range include aging infrastructure existing in a highly corrosive environment that must continue to successfully support missions subject to schedule and requirements variability common on test ranges. These systems are located at WFF, and deployed to sites around the world which sometimes requires simultaneous operations management and staffing. The contractor shall provide timely and reliable systems operations and maintenance while achieving systems performance excellence, continuously improve customer support, and proactively pursue overall cost reductions. The contractor shall ensure system configuration integrity and reliability, mission readiness, and service excellence. ployee safety, and employee training programs. The contractor shall develop and implement an innovative management philosophy to meet evolving mission requirements for the Wallops Range and its customers. Customers include NASA, other Government Agencies and commercial entities with range requirements. The customers’ requirements are defined and provided by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), NASA WFF Range and Mission Management Office, or NASA WFF Project Managers The contractor shall establish, maintain, and implement a Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) to ensure compliance with quality management requirements in this SOW and/or established by the contractor. This effort provides direct customer support to NASA WFF’s Range by providing qualified personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, specialized test equipment, supervision, and other services. NASA’s WFF requires an innovative, integrated, flexible and effective management approach and the contractor must provide technical support in a planned and coordinated manner which will ensure essential Wallops Range support systems are ready to support user requirements, and cause no impact to Wallops Range program schedules due to equipment degradation, failures, system problems or reprioritization of preexisting program requirements. The wide variety of support systems involves flexible workload planning, cost management, and scheduling of resources to identify and resolve technical systems problems. Available capacity for operations, maintenance, and sustaining engineering may be made available to other WFF organizations with the permission of the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), and RMMO Management. Instrumentation systems are permanently located at WFF, Bermuda, and in Alaska. In addition, mobile instrumentation is deployed to locations worldwide, including but not limited to Norway; Kwajalein Atoll; Coquina, NC; Australia; and French Guiana to meet Range customer requirements. The Wallops Range receives and provides Range support from and to various agencies. The Wallops Range constantly strives to ensure it is prepared to accommodate the current and future needs of its customers. AOI 01: EF Technology Sprints - Activated Digital Thread for Battlefield Responsiveness AFRL is seeking innovative solutions to operationalize digital architecture capable of responding to battlefield dynamics in near real-time. The objective is to close the loop between battlefield data and the manufacturing floor, creating an adaptive manufacturing ecosystem that expedites the re-configuration of weapon systems to enhance warfighter lethality. Solutions are sought to drastically reduce design-to-field cycle times by addressing one or more of the following technical challenges: (1) Model-Based Quality Assurance & Digital Certification. Goal: Transition from physical-test-dependent to analysis-led certification. To realize surge manufacturing, the bottleneck of physical requalification for every design change must be eliminated. Solutions are sought that leverage Certification by Analysis (CbA) and probabilistic simulation to validate manufacturing variability and design changes. Approaches should address how seamless data interchange can support certification allowing for rapid acceptance of re-configured components without extensive physical testing campaigns. (2) Modular Integration & Factorial Manufacturing. Goal: Enable "Plug-and-Play"
